rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm ruled prevents: a slide the reader cannot ground because its referent points nowhere the deck has shown them. Checked every pronoun/demonstrative in the new chunk 6 and the two edited chunks (9, 10). Chunk 6 line 54 "A rule in your file is one way to compound a session" — "your file" resolves to `./CLAUDE.local.md`, named three times in the immediately preceding chunk 5 (lines 42, 46, 46). Chunk 6 lines 56-58 pronouns ("it guessed", "the rest", "it again") each resolve to a same-bullet or same-sentence noun. Chunk 6 line 60 "these" resolves to the three just-named bullet categories. Chunk 9 new line 91 "that boundary" resolves within the same sentence ("what it can reach, what it must not touch, and where the blast radius ends"). Chunk 10 new line 105 "a right-sized one" resolves to "one scoped task" in the immediately preceding bolded sentence (line 103), same chunk. No never-named, vague-with-history, or re-chunk-stranded referent found in the diff region. Grep for stray demonstratives (`grep -noE "\b(this|that|these|those|it)\b"`) against the diff lines confirms every hit above is accounted for.

Harm rule prevents: a slide whose meaning depends on where another file's content happens to sit. Chunk 6's two new-adjacent links name their targets directly ("Lecture: Where the rule could live", "Lecture: How instructions grow") — title-named, not located by position, and both lines were already present before this diff (only the section above them is new). No sentence in the diff points at another file by position ("the opening lecture said", "the earlier module"). N/A finding to report against.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm rule prevents: "the X you did" pointing at a beat a re-chunk or rewrite stranded. Chunk 6 line 54 "Anything the plan tripped on" backward-references the plan-mode session the student just ran — confirmed live: `exercises/push-back-on-the-plan.md` and `exercises/extract-the-task-shaping-rule.md` both exist and are linked two chunks earlier (chunk 4, lines 32/34), and the transitions line (maintainer, unchanged in scope but corroborating) places this exact new slide `@after:extract-the-task-shaping-rule`. The referenced beat exists and sits immediately before this slide in delivery order.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: N/A — no guess-then-reveal demo structure anywhere in this file's body; the diff adds a checklist prompt and a reading-list entry, neither shaped as a prediction beat.

Harm rule prevents: a slide that says nothing standalone (a bare wait-state or one context-dependent bullet). Chunk 6 (140 words, 3 bullets per `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file <path> --report`) carries a self-sufficient claim: names the Boy Scout rule, gives three concrete categories with examples, and closes on an actionable prompt. Not an orphan.

Line 52 header "Leave the repo tidier than you found it" is a true summary of its own content: the three bullets (planning gaps, conflicting information, other context) are all repo-tidiness actions, and the closing prompt operationalises exactly that. No header/body contradiction.

Checked all six sub-items against the diff region and the file as a whole. (a) "Not X. Not Y. Z." — `grep -noE "Not [^.]+\.\s+Not [^.]+\."` over the body: zero matches. (b) Anaphora/epistrophe triples — closest candidate is chunk 6's three bullets ("Planning gaps."/"Conflicting information."/"Other context."), but each opens with a distinct handle and distinct sentence structure/content (not a repeated refrain like "Every session..."), so it does not trip this sub-item. (c) Self-grading superlatives — `grep -in "one of the most\|most useful\|most powerful\|most important"` over the body: zero matches. (d) Number + own retraction — the only number-with-hedge in body is line 69's "about 10%", unchanged by this diff and covered by the file's own maintainer accept-note (raw line 121): M1-attested prior, no retraction clause attached, exempted by the rule's own EXCEPT clause. (e) Abstraction-noun stacks — none in the diff; new prose uses concrete nouns ("a file the agent didn't know about", "a comment that contradicts the code", "a script with no usage line"). (f) Verb triplets with an empty leg — none in the diff.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm rule prevents: repo/maintainer authoring jargon (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood) reaching a projected slide where the room can't parse it. Line 54 uses "compound" as a verb ("one way to compound a session") — checked whether this is repo-internal: `grep -rn` across AE101 module bodies (above their own maintainer fences) shows "compound" is arc-earned spine vocabulary taught explicitly from M1 onward — `getting-going.md` LO line 20: "**Compound** the session into a personal rules file at `./CLAUDE.local.md`", plus "the loop is orient → fix → close → compound" (line 57) and repeated body use in `earn-the-trust.md`, `learn-from-the-test.md`. It is the curriculum's own taught term for a real practitioner framework (Kieran Klaassen's "Compound Engineering"), not maintainer/authoring dialect. "Boy Scout rule" (line 54) is a common engineering idiom, and the file's own maintainer block (raw line 125) records it as deliberately unattributed folk usage, not a dialect coinage. "with nothing loaded" (line 54) reuses the file's own established auto-load vocabulary (chunk 5's "are these rules auto-loaded", the Plug Points auto-load list) — student-facing curriculum vocabulary, not repo jargon.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm rule prevents: every bullet opening with a bolded full sentence (the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture), diluting bold's signal value. Chunk 6 carries three bolded spans — "**Planning gaps.**", "**Conflicting information.**", "**Other context.**" — each 2 words, well inside the <=5-word handle cap, each marking a checklist-item name (a content type the rule's own definition explicitly credits as valid handle material: "Bold marks handles only: named laws, governors, coined terms, checklist item names"). The narrative sentence following each bullet is unbolded. This is the handle-not-sentence shape the rule wants, not the banned monoculture. A literal read of "<=1 bolded element on most slides" would count 3 here, but the rule's own carve-out ("a law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law") already grants multiple handles when a slide's whole job is naming several parallel items — see rule_questions for whether that carve-out's wording should say so explicitly for checklists too.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: New chunk 6 ("## Leave the repo tidier than you found it") is plain top-level module prose, not wrapped in any `<!--flag:module:X-->` / `<!--flag:no-module:X-->` pair (verified: `grep -n "flag:" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/plan-mode-done-right.md` shows the nearest flags are at lines 85/93/97/99/101/107, all bracketing the Pre-reads/Next sections, none touching lines 52-67). Module body reaches the composed deck via the top-level `section.module` wrapper (per rule 10's own text), so this slide is present in every cut. `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file <path> --report` independently confirms it as one of the file's 10 measured slides, so the size-check tooling (which also resolves runtime forks through the renderer) sees it too.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mechanical, both runtime-fork branches checked. `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file <path> --report`: 10 slides, 0 oversized; new chunk 6 measures 140 words / 3 bullets (largest new slide, well under cap). The script's default run resolves the module-present branch of the ## Next fork (46 words). The module-ABSENT branch (containing the diff's new "test for a right-sized one" paragraph) is not covered by that default flag resolution, so it was checked by hand: extracted the `<!--flag:no-module:earn-the-trust-->` block and ran a word/bullet count — 125 words, 0 bullets, also well under 210/6.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule's own text splits only two file kinds — "Exercise `##` headings = imperative or phase label" / "Lecture headings = claims" — plus named non-violation categories (orientation headers, catalogue entries, phase/section labels). This target is a MODULE file; its own custom section headings (`## Save the rule if it earned itself`, `## Leave the repo tidier than you found it`) are neither an included exercise's nor an included lecture's headings, and the rule states no grammar requirement for a module's own section headers. New header "Leave the repo tidier than you found it" reads as an orientation/label heading in the same family as the file's other module-level custom headings, not a governed exercise-imperative or lecture-claim slot.

rule_questions: Rule 9's only stated multi-handle carve-out is "a law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law," but the rule's own handle definition also lists "checklist item names" as valid bold content. `## Leave the repo tidier than you found it` bolds three 2-word checklist-item names (Planning gaps / Conflicting information / Other context) — same shape as the law carve-out (one short handle per named item), not the banned every-bullet-bold-sentence monoculture. Should the carve-out say "a law/consolidation OR checklist slide may carry one handle per item," so a future judge doesn't have to reason this from the handle-definition sentence each time?
